title: Conversant API Tunnel — spec journal
content:
Context:
This is a personal journal/sketch for a lightweight 'Conversant' API Tunnel concept: a thin, multi-tenant, multiplexed API tunnel intended to carry small control messages, prefetch bundles, and resume checkpoints between clients (mobile/web) and the Redwood edge/ingress.

Goal (high level):
- Provide a single long-lived connection that supports: incremental prompt push, small KV-style checkpoint upload/download, resume handshake, lightweight tool-calls, and telemetry pipelining.
- Low operational cost: run on existing ingress fleet (envoy/nginx) with minimal new state.
- Good for intermittent connectivity (mobile): enables resumable sessions and prewarm hints.

Constraints / assumptions:  
- Client can open a single HTTP/2 (prefer h2 over TLS) connection per logical device.
- Messages are small (<= 64KB typical); large artifacts still via signed S3 URLs.
- Prefer not to require persistent per-session storage on ingress; keep session state in KV backend (Dynamo/Consul) or pass-through to runtime.
- Keep auth simple: bearer token + short-lived device-attestation header.

Design tradeoffs noted: 
- Multiplexed streams vs many short-lived HTTP requests: multiplexing reduces TLS handshake overhead on mobile but introduces stream management complexity.
- Do we trust client order? No — server must re-sequence by sequence numbers for idempotent operations.

API shapes (sketch):
- Connection: POST /v1/tunnel/connect  (upgrade optional)
  - Request headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  - Required headers: x-device-id, x-client-version, x-timestamp
  - Response 200: { tunnel_id, server_nonce, recommended-heartbeat_s }

- Framing model: each HTTP/2 stream carries a JSON envelope with fields: 
  { "t": "msg_type", "sid": "stream_session_id", "seq": 42, "payload": "base64|plain depending on type" }
  msg_type values: prefetch_bundle, checkpoint_put, checkpoint_get, resume_request, resume_ack, telemetry, tool_call, control

Example prefetch_bundle envelope:
{
  "t": "prefetch_bundle",
  "sid": "session:userid:random",
  "seq": 17,
  "payload": "{\"prompts\": [{\"id\": \"p1\",\"text\": \"Summarize last messages\"}], \"hint_profile\": \"low-latency\" }"
}

- Checkpoint PUT: client streams a small binary blob (gzip) with metadata headers: checkpoint-version, ttl-seconds, model-hint. Server responds 201 with checkpoint-id.
- Checkpoint GET: client requests checkpoint by id; server returns 200 with Content-Encoding: gzip and metadata headers.

Handshake / resume flow (ASCII sequence):
client -> POST /v1/tunnel/connect -> 200 {tunnel_id}
(client opens stream1) -> SEND {t:resume_request, sid:s1, seq:1, payload:{checkpoint_ids:[c123], last_ack:42}}
server -> validates token, queries checkpoint store -> replies on same stream: {t:resume_ack, sid:s1, seq:1, payload:{accepted:true, events:[{type:prompt, id:p89}]}}
If accepted -> server can open server-initiated stream to push prewarm prefetch bundle (server-initiated h2 stream).

Multiplexing details / stream lifecycle notes:
- Each logical 'session' (user conversation) gets a short-lived sid; sid collision protection via random suffix.
- seq must be monotonic per sid; server ignores lower/equal seq (idempotency).
- TTL for sids: ephemeral, server can garbage-collect after inactivity window (configurable, default 10m).

Telemetry and tracing: 
- Each envelope includes trace-context header: traceparent or x-rw-span-id.
- Suggested minimal telemetry events: connect, stream-open, stream-close, resume-accept, checkpoint-put, checkpoint-get, prefetch-apply, auth-failure.
- Emit sample telemetry to console and to per-route metrics (console: per-client token, region).

Auth and trust model: 
- Primary: standard Redwood API key/bearer tokens.
- Device attestation header (optional) for sensitive tenants: x-device-attest: base64(signed-claims).
- Token scope: tokens enumerate allowed actions (prefetch, checkpoint, telemetry). Servers must reject unauthorized message types.

Failure modes and recovery: 
- Connection drop: client reconnects and replays resume_request with last_ack. Server is responsible for de-duping.
- Mid-stream failure: client retries stream with new seq; server must be idempotent.
- Stale checkpoint: server returns 410 with suggested recovery flow (recompute, full-reupload).

Operational concerns: 
- Ingress memory: avoid per-connection in-memory queues; use streaming hand-off to worker pool or persistent queue (kafka) if backlog occurs.
- Backpressure: clients send x-backpressure-window header and server may return 429 when limits reached.
- Rate limiting: per-token, per-device limits; prefer token-based quotas for fairness.

Edge cases / TODOs: 
- Do we support binary streaming (for voice) over the same tunnel? probably no in v1.
- Hot migration: how to move tunnel handling from one ingress node to another without client re-open? maybe sticky routing via HAProxy cookies.
- Transparent fallback to short HTTP POST if h2 unsupported.

Experiment plan (mini):
1) Build h2-only PoC handler in runtime-proxy that accepts the envelope format, stores checkpoints in s3, and replays simple resume flows. (1 engineer, 2 weeks)
2) Wire telemetry events and a small simulated mobile client that does connect/resume with intermittent disconnects.
3) Run a 48-hour stress test: 10k simulated devices connecting every minute and doing checkpoint_put/get operations. Measure ingress mem, streams per connection, tail latencies.

Sample lightweight server-side pseudocode (very rough):

on_connect(req):
  validate_bearer(req.headers[Authorization])
  tunnel = create_tunnel_record(req.headers[x-device-id], req.client_ip)"
  return {tunnel_id: tunnel.id}"

on_stream(stream):
  env = json_parse(stream.read_all())
  if not allowed(env.t): return error(403)
  if env.t == 'checkpoint_put': store_checkpoint(env.sid, env.seq, stream.body)
  elif env.t == 'resume_request': result = reconcile_resume(env)"
  respond_on_stream(stream.id, result)

Notes-to-self: keep envelope tiny; avoid embedding entire prompts in base64 if not necessary. I like the idea of small JSON metadata + signed S3 urls for payloads > 8KB.

Open questions: 
- TTL policies and billing implications: should checkpoint storage be billable to customers per-MB? need product input.
- How to surface 'prefetch hints' into Optimize engine to suggest quantization/profile changes? (hook in Optimize -> per-route suggestions).

Related threads / references: 
- Prior convo: slack thread GqY2p9f about session warmup costs.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/tunnels PR#187 — implements initial h2 connect handshake.
- Jira: CON-3421 backpressure and quotas epic.

Final rough checklist: 
- [ ] PoC server + client
- [ ] Basic checkpoint PUT/GET implemented (s3 backend)
- [ ] Telemetry events wired to console and ingestion
- [ ] Integration test for resume de-dup
- [ ] Doc: public API shape for client SDK

Random thoughts:
- Could piggyback small token refresh on the tunnel itself to reduce separate auth calls (server issues short-lived refresh on connect). Consider security implications.
- Might be attractive as a low-latency alternative to frequent polling for mobile; measure battery/cpu impact.

Version history:
- 2025-01-12 initial notes
- 2025-01-20 added handshake flow and seq semantics
- 2025-02-04 added experiment plan and TODOs

End of jotter.
